senses.definition: To ask someone to share what they have learned, in an informal conversation.
senses.caution: It sounds casual while asking for open-ended time, and the whole cost falls on them. Sent cold to someone senior with no boundary on it - no length, no topic, no reason it has to be them - it reads as entitled, and to some it reads as asking them to do your thinking. Put twenty minutes and a specific question around it and it becomes easy to say yes to. The register is informal: right in a message to a colleague, wrong in a first approach to an MD you have never met.
senses.example: You've done two of these migrations. Could I pick your brain for twenty minutes before we commit to a design?

cues.text: A colleague has already done two migrations like the one you are starting, and you want half an hour of informal conversation rather than a document from them.
You are messaging someone in another department whose experience you need, and you want a phrase that makes the request sound small and easy to accept.
A friend of a friend has renovated a flat like yours and you want an hour of their time and, more usefully, their mistakes.
Your cousin has just been through the visa process you are about to start, and you want to sit down with them and ask everything.

distractors: To make something deliberately hard to follow.
To put right something that was wrong.
To rework the exact phrasing of a draft without changing what it says.
To dig patiently through records for something nobody hid but nobody wrote up either.
To back a claim with evidence that somebody other than you can go and check it.
